Long-term conversational agents need to remember and query
cross-session, multi-typed information with complex correlations.
Existing agent memory systems rely on heterogeneous vector and
graph databases, which fragment memory information and cause
high cross-database I/O latency. For retrieval, common RAG-style
methods tend to introduce noise, miss correlated clues, and lack
token budget control, degrading LLM accuracy and efficiency.

solidates fragmented memory representations and storage into a
unified memory-native architecture. Its core components include:

abstract layer that agglomerates basic memories into traceable ab-

Existing systems combine vector databases, graph databases, and
other databases, which fragment memory and force hybrid queries
to cross database boundaries with high I/O and serialization over-
head. Guided by the hierarchical memory model, Mandol replaces
this architecture with an agglomerative semantic data structure
composed ofSemanticMapandSemanticGraph, which natively fuses
key-value storage, vector indexes, and graph topology within a
single address space. Figure 2 shows how these semantic data struc-
tures support both unified storage and the downstream quantitative
retrieval pipeline. The left side corresponds to the in-memory or-
ganization, while the right side corresponds to the retrieval stages
introduced in Section 3.3.

evidence.excerpt:
SemanticMap and SemanticGraph form a unified stor-
age view, physically realizing the structured semantic graph and
eliminating multi-database fragmentation.
To support flexible retrieval, the system provides a set of atomic
hybrid operators that natively operate on SemanticMap and Seman-
ticGraph, covering unit, space, relationship, and multi-hop queries.
These operators can be composed into complex retrieval plans and
are detailed in Section 4. The active memory layer connects to an
underlying embedded persistence backend, DuckDB, for cold or
long-term storage through the asynchronous paging mechanism
described in Section 4.

evidence.excerpt:
brid recall, the candidate set faces two issues: intra-source noise,
where semantic relevance scores follow a long-tail distribution with
weakly relevant memories scattered in the low-score region, and
cross-source conflicts, where different sources may describe the
same event or stale abstractions contradict newer evidence. Mandol
addresses both in two stages.
Intra-source denoising.Traditional static thresholds or methods
based on mean and standard deviation assume a specific score dis-
tribution and are easily disturbed by extremely high or low scores,
causing unstable filtering. Since different queries can produce non-
normal score distributions, we apply a dynamic threshold based
on the median absolute deviation (MAD), which robustly filters
low-scoring noisy candidates without assuming normality:
𝜏𝑚𝑎𝑑 =median(𝑆 𝑐𝑒)−𝜅·MAD(𝑆 𝑐𝑒),(1)

The latency advantage mainly comes from three factors. First,
many existing memory systems rely on external database services,
so each query requires serialization, database execution, result
transfer, and parsing before the Python-side pipeline can continue.
This database round trip becomes a substantial overhead on the
serving path. Second, multi-store systems further introduce cross-
database orchestration overhead, such as retrieving candidates from
a vector store and then issuing additional filtering, expansion, or
relation queries to a graph or relational store. These steps increase
both tail latency and mean latency. Third, Mandol adopts an in-
process memory architecture, where retrieval indexes, structured
memory links, and active memory states are

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Retrieved contexts are validated through end-to-end question answering against benchmark ground truth using separate LLM judges, and system performance is measured by objective API-level latency profiling.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcomes are established by downstream QA accuracy on LoCoMo and LongMemEval using GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini answer generation with an LLM-based correctness script, plus direct wall-clock latency measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The retrieval pipeline is shaped by static pretrained retrieval models (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and bge-reranker-v2-m3) plus hand-designed heuristic scoring formulas such as MAD thresholding, exponential time decay, and MMR.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of superior retrieval accuracy, lower token consumption, and substantial latency reductions (e.g., 5.4x search speedup, 4.8x add speedup under 10 QPS) are supported by comparative tables and profiling across server and consumer hardware.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation covers both task quality across two established long-context conversational benchmarks (LoCoMo and LongMemEval) with multiple LLM generation backbones, and systems-level measurements (P99/P90/mean search and insertion latencies, RAM/GPU footprint). Mandol consistently outperforms standard baselines like Mem0, Zep, and EverMemOS in both accuracy and speed.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Retrieved contexts are assessed through end-to-end question answering evaluated on benchmark ground truth using independent LLM judges, alongside wall-clock API latency measurements.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream QA task accuracy evaluated on external benchmarks (LoCoMo and LongMemEval) via established GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini evaluation scripts, as well as direct system latency profiling.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-trained static retrieval models (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and bge-reranker-v2-m3) combined with heuristic scoring formulas (MAD thresholding, exponential time decay, and MMR).

primary.limitations: The manuscript identifies that high-level memory extraction depends on an LLM during offline ingestion and notes slight underperformance on specific subtasks against models with significantly larger embedding and reranker backbones.
primary.method_assessment: The system design is thoroughly documented with clear architectural layers, explicit formulas for MAD thresholding and cross-source conflict resolution, and detailed API designs backed by embedded DuckDB persistence. Retrieval executes entirely via non-LLM algorithmic operations, eliminating runtime model inference overhead.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript provides a sound systems-oriented contribution addressing latency and fragmentation bottlenecks in LLM agent memory architectures. The empirical evidence across established conversational benchmarks and thorough systems benchmarking is complete and robust.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Mandol, an in-process, memory-native long-term agent memory system integrating a hierarchical structured semantic graph, in-memory unified data structures (SemanticMap and SemanticGraph), and an LLM-free quantitative retrieval mechanism featuring adaptive routing, MAD-based denoising, freshness arbitration, and MMR-based context selection.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript provides a sound systems-oriented contribution addressing latency and fragmentation bottlenecks in LLM agent memory architectures. The empirical evidence across established conversational benchmarks and thorough systems benchmarking is complete and robust.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript identifies that high-level memory extraction depends on an LLM during offline ingestion and notes slight underperformance on specific subtasks against models with significantly larger embedding and reranker backbones.
